headline: NVIDIA'S CALIFORNIA BUYERS
dek: A CBS News investigation found two California companies with priority access to Nvidia's most advanced chips are owned by Chinese firms.

graphic.title: WHO OWNS THE BUYERS · PER CBS NEWS

steps.name: NVIDIA
steps.sub: Sells its most advanced AI chips

steps.name: RICLOUD AI
steps.sub: San Jose, Calif. · Nvidia “preferred” cloud partner

steps.name: YUXING INFOTECH
steps.sub: Parent company · Shenzhen, China · Hong Kong-listed

chains.note: Nvidia's filings count these as U.S. sales. This year RiCloud agreed to lease 300 Nvidia B300 servers to a Taiwan firm once known for importing whisky.
chains.status: The U.S. government has not accused RiCloud or Yuxing of wrongdoing.

steps.name: NVIDIA
steps.sub: Lists Aivres as an “elite” partner, its top tier

steps.name: AIVRES
steps.sub: California server maker · formerly named Inspur

steps.name: INSPUR
steps.sub: Chinese parent · Inspur group firms blacklisted by the U.S. in March 2023

chains.note: Aivres renamed itself after that blacklisting. It shipped servers with Blackwell chips to firms in Malaysia, including Megaspeed, a New York Times analysis found.
chains.status: Aivres itself is not blacklisted. It did not respond to CBS.

means.label: Bought in the U.S.:
means.text: These chips are sold to U.S.-based companies. CBS does not report that any of these sales broke export rules.

means.label: Vetting questions:
means.text: Nvidia has not said what background checks it ran before giving RiCloud partner status, CBS reports.

means.label: What's next:
means.text: Sen. Chris Coons, in line to chair Senate Foreign Relations, is poised to investigate workarounds to China chip bans.

sources: Sources: CBS News investigation (Josh Boswell), Nov. 25, 2026, citing corporate filings, court records, Nvidia partner listings and filings, and ownership research by C4ADS; New York Times trade-records analysis, as cited by CBS.
